description: FIRST MIDPOINT-CONSTRAINT GOLDEN (SKETCH-VOCAB-1): the audit's own example — a hole placed on the CENTRE of an edge rather than at a typed coordinate (docs/AUDIT-PRODUCT.md T-5). A 40 x 25 x 10 mm plate carries a construction diagonal from (0,0) to (40,25), pinned at both ends, and a R6 hole drawn off-centre at (14, 8) whose CENTRE is midpoint-constrained to that diagonal — so the constraint, and only the constraint, puts it at (20, 12.5). The golden fails if midpoint is a no-op (the hole stays at (14,8) and the centroid moves off the plate centre), and it fails if only the point-on-line half is wired (the hole slides along the diagonal to somewhere that is not its middle). It also locks that CONSTRUCTION geometry stays out of the profile: the diagonal crosses the plate, and a solid built from it would not be a plate with one hole at all.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug).

solved sketch: the four outline lines carry no constraints and start at their analytic positions, so they come back bitwise. The construction diagonal is fixed at both ends, so its midpoint is ((0+40)/2, (0+25)/2) = (20, 12.5), and the midpoint constraint puts the hole centre exactly there. The radius dimension holds r = 6.

surface_area = 2*(1000 - pi*6^2)  [top + bottom faces, each pierced by the hole]  + 2*(40+25)*10  [four outer side walls]  + 2*pi*6*10  [the cylindrical hole wall]  = 1773.8053289415349 + 1300 + 376.99111843077515 = 3450.79644737231 mm^2

centroid = (20, 12.5, 5) mm: the midpoint of the plate's own diagonal IS the plate's centre, so the hole is central and removing it preserves the full-plate centroid. That is what makes this golden's centroid a direct read-out of the constraint under test.
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[40,25,10]: the hole is interior (r = 6 at (20,12.5) reaches x 14..26, y 6.5..18.5) and the construction line is not part of the solid

topology: 7 faces (top + bottom plate faces, 4 outer side walls, 1 cylindrical hole wall), 15 edges (top boundary = 4 rect edges + 1 hole circle = 5; bottom = 5; 4 vertical box corner edges; 1 vertical seam edge on the periodic hole cylinder), 1 shell — i.e. exactly the one-hole plate, with no trace of the construction diagonal.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, isRelative=False): the hole circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments (a function of the ANGULAR deflection alone, so the same count at any radius). Periodic hole cylinder = (126+1)*2 = 254 nodes, 126*2 = 252 triangles. Each plate cap has a rectangular outer loop (4 nodes) + one 126-gon hole = 130 boundary nodes, triangulated with one hole to 130 - 2 + 2*1 = 130 triangles; two caps = 260 nodes / 260 triangles. Four rectangular side walls = 4 * (4 nodes, 2 tris) = 16 nodes / 8 triangles. Totals = 530 vertices and 520 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces).
no material is assigned, so mass and centre of mass must be reported ABSENT (null) — never 0 g (docs/design/materials.md 6)
GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned: asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but the absolute size carries no geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: MEASURED first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). A midpoint between two FIXED endpoints is an average of two exact numbers, so — like the diameter golden and unlike the angle one, whose apex is the output of an iterative solve — the solver contributes essentially nothing here and the residual error is the kernel's wire->face->prism path. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-08-26, planegcs 0.8.0 / build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9): volume exactly 0.0, surface_area 4.5e-13 mm^2, centroid <= 3.6e-15 mm, AABB exactly 0.0 on all six bounds. The documented ceiling 1e-9 is the same posture and the same number as the sketch-extrude and plate-with-holes goldens whose construction path this one shares, and it stays 1e5 x TIGHTER than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m = 1e-4 mm). Loosening it is never a fix for a red run: it is a reviewed kernel-level decision recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
